You said:
What does idempotent mean for a data load?

ChatGPT said:
An idempotent load gives the same result whether it runs once or many times. Running it twice must not create duplicates.

You said:
So retrying a failed load makes it idempotent?

ChatGPT said:
Not quite. Retrying is only safe if the load is already idempotent. A plain INSERT retried after a partial failure can double-count rows.

You said:
Explain it simpler, give me an example

ChatGPT said:
Think of a light switch set to "on". Pressing "set to on" twice leaves it on. A toggle pressed twice turns it off. Loads should behave like "set to on": MERGE on a key, or delete-then-insert a partition.

You said:
I still don't get how MERGE makes the load idempotent again

ChatGPT said:
MERGE matches incoming rows to existing rows by key. Matched rows are updated, new rows are inserted, so a rerun updates the same rows instead of adding copies.

You said:
What is a watermark in streaming?

ChatGPT said:
A watermark is the engine's estimate of how far event time has progressed, used to decide when late data can be dropped.

You said:
Thanks, write that as a table
